categories.name: Desk Tools
categories.blurb: Precision instruments for people who measure twice.

items.name: Machined Aluminium Ruler
items.blurb: A 300 mm rule milled from a single billet.
items.description: Milled from a single billet of 6061 aluminium and anodised to a soft graphite finish. The engraved scale is filled with white epoxy so it stays legible after years of desk use. Non-slip cork backing keeps it where you put it.

image.alt: Machined aluminium ruler lying flat on a plain background

items.name: Brass Pen Rest
items.blurb: A small weight that keeps a pen exactly where you left it.
items.description: Turned from solid brass and left unlacquered, so it darkens slowly with handling. The shallow groove holds anything from a fine liner to a fountain pen without rolling. Felt base, 180 grams.

image.alt: Small brass pen rest photographed from a low angle

items.name: Folding Steel Bookstand
items.blurb: Holds a reference book open at a readable angle.
items.description: Powder-coated spring steel that folds flat to eleven millimetres and opens to three fixed angles. Rated for a hardback of up to two kilograms, with silicone pads front and back so nothing slides or scuffs.

image.alt: Folding steel bookstand shown open at its middle angle

items.name: Cork Desk Mat
items.blurb: Six millimetres of cork, cut to a generous working size.
items.description: Pressed from granulated Portuguese cork and sealed with a water-based finish that resists coffee rings. Warm underhand, quiet under a keyboard, and light enough to roll up when the desk needs clearing.

image.alt: Rectangular cork desk mat viewed from directly above

categories.name: Board games
categories.blurb: Games that earn their shelf space and survive a hundred plays.

items.name: Hexwood Trading Company
items.blurb: A two-hour trading game for three to five players.
items.description: A route-building game across a forested island, played on interlocking hex tiles that shuffle into a new map each time. The wooden goods markers are screen-printed rather than stickered, so they survive shuffling. Teaches in about ten minutes and lasts around two hours.

image.alt: Board game box beside a partly assembled hex tile map

items.name: Lantern Street
items.blurb: A quiet tile-laying game for two.
items.description: Two players build adjacent streets from the same shrinking pool of tiles, each trying to light more windows than the other. Plays in twenty-five minutes and fits in a coat pocket. The tiles are 2 mm greyboard with a linen finish.

image.alt: Small two-player tile game with tiles laid out in a street pattern

items.name: The Longest Winter
items.blurb: A cooperative survival game for one to four players.
items.description: A cooperative game about rationing supplies through a winter that lasts twelve rounds. Every player sees the same dwindling stores, and the game is lost together or not at all. Includes a solo mode that changes the card deck rather than the rules.

image.alt: Cooperative board game laid out mid-game with resource cards and tokens

items.name: Pocket Draughts Set
items.blurb: A magnetic travel set in a folding walnut case.
items.description: A folding walnut case that opens into a full draughts board, with magnetic pieces that stay put on a train table. Closed it is roughly the size of a paperback. The hinge is brass and replaceable.

image.alt: Folding walnut draughts set open to show the magnetic board and pieces
